## CELL FACTS

Cell 金_伤官 (Metal carrying The Virtuoso). Persona The Virtuoso (伤官). Definition line: "Cross-current output, brilliance made of what it meets". Keyword Brilliance, charge fierce, poles catalyst Spark / friction Pushback. Family function: Expression. Cost dimension: brilliance against the grain; shining reads as defiance. Arena: the stage, spark, off-script, the note held too long. Classical portrait: brilliance and defiance; output that exceeds its container; 傲物气高, cannot hold its tongue. Ruled domains: Talent, Performance, Defiance. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 食神.
Element arena: Metal (edge, blade, ore, forge, whetstone, the clean line). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Earth. structural_interaction seed: "Earth generating Metal cross-polarity — precision that structurally exceeds its container".
- k2_overview: "Your Metal moves as the Virtuoso: an edge that performs. You cut with style, argue like a fencing match, and produce work so sharp it draws blood and applause in the same stroke. Standards bore you unless you set them. Authority irritates you unless it earned itself. The world calls it attitude. It is precision refusing dullness."
- k2_functional: "Your wit cuts clean and quotable. People fear your reviews and collect them."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Razor-witted","Piercing","Masterful"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Talent":"Your talent is the brilliant edge: work with finish other people cannot reach. Sign it, show it, price it properly. Metal brilliance that stays sheathed reads as arrogance without the receipts.","Performance":"You perform with precision: the flawless delivery, the duel won in public. Choose stages where exactness shines, competitions, critiques, crafts. Applause for sharpness is the kind you can actually live on.","Defiance":"Your defiance is the refusal to dull: standards no supervisor can lower, corners you will not round. Aim it at shoddiness rather than at every hand holding a clipboard. Rebellion with a portfolio wins."}

- Sibling cell 金_食神 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Craft-loving","Refined","Savoring"],"friction":["Fussy","Self-satisfied","Dulled"]}
- Sibling cell 金_食神 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "The right way has become the only way, and the tolerances keep narrowing. The coffee is drinkable at one temperature, the towels fold along one axis, the restaurant loses you at the first wobbling table. Quality was the point once. The specifications have since annexed the pleasure."

Core element Earth, energy element Metal. Law: Earth feeds Metal (土生金: ore grows in the mountain). Relative to the core the energy is the fed, so Metal is this core's Expression. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Earth core that shows Metal on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Metal as the Expression is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. value.text: Direct is the only setting you have for the truth. A softened answer feels like a lie you would have to keep up, so you say it exactly rather than gently. Keep in mind that you can say it slowly, and slowly is kinder.

value.text: Given an instruction, you talk back in front of everyone. Having the last word feels more like respect to you than taking the note, and you make whoever is above you defend a small request. Remember to save the talking back for what matters.

value.text: Grading people is something you do without meaning to. A quick read of someone's worth feels safer than not knowing, so you grade them on sight rather than wait to be surprised. It is worth remembering that you grade yourself the same way.

value_b.text: You know what you think of someone before they finish talking. Having no grade for someone feels like having no floor, and you grade early and defend it rather than change it. It is worth remembering that you get the early grades wrong most often.

value.text: Grading someone costs you what they know. Since you would rather be right about a person than learn from them, you stop listening at the grade. You learn nothing from someone you have graded, and that is the part to remember.

value.text: When you meet someone, you grade them before you greet them. The fast read feels more honest than the slow one, and you give people the grade instead of your attention. You leave them more chance to surprise you when you grade in pencil.
